points.description: Describes mRNA leaving the nucleus through a nuclear pore and travelling through the cytoplasm to a ribosome (or to the rough endoplasmic reticulum). Equivalent wording earns the mark.
Describes decoding: mRNA is read in triplet codons, and a tRNA whose anticodon is complementary to the codon (U with A, C with G) binds to it. Equivalent wording earns the mark.

Describes linking amino acids into a polypeptide: each tRNA's amino acid is bonded to the growing chain, adding amino acids one at a time from a START codon until a STOP codon is read. Equivalent wording earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks for a student who gives all three ideas, using any equivalent wording, even if they name the stages differently (e.g. transport, translation/decoding, elongation/termination). Award 0 for each idea not present; the question asks for four steps but only 3 marks are available, so award marks for the ideas above rather than counting steps.
